# Write marketing emails fast with Cohere’s text generation

Tired of staring at a blank screen while you try to craft a sales email? By the end of this guide you’ll be able to feed Cohere a few simple instructions and walk away with a ready‑to‑send subject line and body that sound just like your brand. This is for anyone who wants a quick, reliable writing boost without needing any code.

## Before you start
- A free Cohere account (sign‑up at cohere.com).  
- A web browser on a laptop, desktop, or tablet with an internet connection.  
- A clear idea of the product or service you want to promote (one sentence is enough).  
- About 5 minutes total – the guide is designed to be completed in a short coffee break.  

## Step 1 — Sign in and open the Cohere Playground  
Open your web browser and go to **cohere.com**. Click the **Log in** button in the top‑right corner (it looks like a small person icon). After you log in you’ll see a dashboard with tiles such as “Playground”, “Projects”, and “Documentation”. Click the tile labeled **Playground** – it may also appear as a button that says “Try the Playground”. The Playground opens a clean text area where you can type prompts and watch the AI reply. If you don’t see a Playground tile, look for a menu icon (three horizontal lines) and choose “Playground” from the list.  
💬 Example: none needed for this step – just click.  
You’ll know it worked when a blank white box with a cursor appears, ready for you to type.

## Step 2 — Write a prompt that tells Cohere who you are and what tone you need  
In the text box, type a **prompt** (the instruction you give to an AI, like a brief you hand to a copywriter). Explain the product, the offer, and the voice you want. For instance, write:  
> “Write a short marketing email for a local organic fruit and vegetable delivery service called **Fresh Harvest**. Announce a new weekly box subscription, offer a 10 % discount for the first month, and keep the tone warm, friendly, and helpful.”  
When you press **Enter** or click the **Generate** button below the box, Cohere’s large language model (LLM – a computer program that predicts text like the engine behind ChatGPT) will start producing a response. If the button looks different, it may be a blue “Submit” or a paper‑plane icon; click whatever appears to send your prompt.  
💬 Example: copy the sentence above exactly into the box.  
You’ll know it worked when the screen fills with a subject line and several paragraphs of email copy.

## Step 3 — Review the first draft and note what needs tweaking  
The AI’s reply will usually include a subject line on the first line, followed by a blank line, then the email body. Read it carefully; check that the product name, discount amount, and tone match what you asked for. If the subject line is too long, or the body feels too formal, you’ll need to ask for a revision. Remember, Cohere can draft text but **cannot send the email for you** – you still have to copy the result into your email client. If the layout looks different (for example, the reply appears in a side panel rather than under the prompt), scroll down until you see the generated text.  
💬 Example: none needed – just read.  
You’ll know it worked when you can see both a subject line and at least three paragraphs of body text.

## Step 4 — Refine the tone with a follow‑up prompt  
Below the first answer, there’s another text box for a new prompt. Type a short instruction that asks the AI to adjust the style, for example:  
> “Make the email sound a bit more relaxed and casual. Use Australian spelling such as ‘favor’ and ‘organize’, and shorten the subject line to under six words.”  
Press **Generate** again. The AI will produce a revised version that follows your additional guidance. If the button for generating a second answer is hidden, look for a small “+” icon next to the original prompt or a “Regenerate” link – clicking either will send the new instruction.  
💬 Example: copy the sentence above exactly.  
You’ll know it worked when the new output shows a shorter, punchier subject line and the body uses the requested spelling variations.

## Step 5 — Copy the finished email into your favorite email client  
Select the entire subject line and body text (click and drag, then press **Ctrl + C** on Windows or **Cmd + C** on macOS). Open your email program (Gmail, Outlook, etc.) and start a new message. Paste the copied text into the subject field (**Ctrl + V** / **Cmd + V**) and the body area. Make any final personal touches – for example, add the recipient’s name or a signature block. If you don’t see a paste option, right‑click in the field and choose “Paste”.  
💬 Example: none – just use the copy‑and‑paste shortcuts.  
You’ll know it worked when the email draft in your client shows the exact subject line and body you generated, ready to hit “Send”.

## Common mistakes
- **Using a vague prompt:** Writing “write a sales email” leaves the AI guessing and often produces generic copy. Fix it by always including the product name, the specific offer, and the desired tone.  
- **Forgetting to edit the AI output:** The generated text may contain placeholders like “[Your Name]”. Always replace those with real details before sending.  
- **Assuming the AI can send the email:** Cohere only creates the wording; you must manually copy the result into your email platform and press send.  

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** You can quickly draft polite RSVP messages, community newsletters, or club updates without breaking a sweat.  
- **For your business or work:** Generate whole weeks of promotional emails, newsletters, and even social‑media captions in a single session, freeing up hours for strategy instead of writing.  
- **If you're just getting started:** Treat the prompt as a conversation – you can keep refining until the copy feels just right, no need for a perfect first try.  

## Try it now  
Open the Cohere Playground, paste the “Fresh Harvest” prompt from Step 2, hit Generate, and watch the AI give you a ready‑to‑use email draft. You’ll have a complete marketing email in under two minutes – give it a go!
